notes: Shelf Blood pressure: 4 old kinds became 2. 'Wearable blood-pressure monitor' (k44) is now the 'Wearable' type, and 'Blood-pressure monitor cuff' (k46) is now a spare-parts note in t of Blood-pressure monitor. I cut the 14 old monitor models to 10, all from the named makers. Each model's label gives its status on the STRIDE BP home-monitor list (stridebp.org/home-pdf, retrieved this session, generated 25 Oct 2026), plus any Consumer Reports top pick or Which? test. I could not see the Which? Best Buy verdicts because they are behind a login, so models are marked 'Which? tested' only. The US Validated Device Listing (validatebp.org) could not be fetched, so US validation status is not recorded. I dropped these: Omron HeartGuide (not on the STRIDE list; the wearable type covers it), Garmin Index BPM (not on the STRIDE list), the Beurer US-named models (Auto 400, Deluxe 600, Premium 800/800W, Elite 900), Withings BPM Vision, Omron Complete (an ECG combo, better under the ECG shelf) and Omron 5/10 Series. I also dropped the two Omron replacement-cuff SKUs, including the professional HEM-907XL clinic cuff, which is out of scope. The Omron numbered-Series range is folded into the Omron brand-register lines. The STRIDE list does not record whether 'Omron 7 Series BP6350' and 'Braun ExactFit 3' match a validated device, so they are marked 'not matched'. Manual kit: kept the Veridian ProKit; its source is now the Wikipedia Sphygmomanometer article. Suggestion for the department note: validation standard = AAMI/ESH/ISO 81060-2:2018 (STRIDE BP, BIHS, US VDL lists).
